sourceUnits.zh: 慕容皝
sourceUnits.en: Murong Huang.
sourceUnits.literal: Murong Huang.

sourceUnits.zh: 慕容皝，字元真，廆第三子也。
sourceUnits.en: Murong Huang, whose courtesy name was Yuanzhen, was Murong Hui’s third son.
sourceUnits.literal: Murong Huang, courtesy name Yuanzhen, was the third son of Murong Hui.

sourceUnits.zh: 龍顏版齒，身長七尺八寸。
sourceUnits.en: He had an imperial bearing, unusually square teeth, and stood seven feet eight inches tall.
sourceUnits.literal: Dragon face and “plaque” teeth; body height seven chi eight cun.

sourceUnits.zh: 雄毅多權略，尚經學，善天文。
sourceUnits.en: He was bold, resourceful, devoted to the classics, and adept at reading the stars.
sourceUnits.literal: Heroic and resolute, abundant in stratagem; esteemed classical learning; skilled in astronomy.

sourceUnits.zh: 廆為遼東公，立為世子。
sourceUnits.en: When Murong Hui was named duke of Liaodong, Huang was made his heir.
sourceUnits.literal: When Hui became Duke of Liaodong, he was established as heir apparent.

sourceUnits.zh: 建武初，拜為冠軍將軍、左賢王，封望平侯，率眾征討，累有功。
sourceUnits.en: Early in the Jianwu era he was named general who champions the army and left worthy prince, created marquis of Wangping, and led troops on several successful expeditions.
sourceUnits.literal: At the beginning of Jianwu, appointed General Who Champions the Army, Left Worthy Prince, enfeoffed Marquis of Wangping; led host in campaigns; repeatedly had merit.

sourceUnits.zh: 太甯末，拜平北將軍，進封朝鮮公。
sourceUnits.en: Late in the Taining era he became general who pacifies the north and was promoted to duke of Chaoxian.
sourceUnits.literal: At the end of Taining, appointed General Who Pacifies the North; advanced enfeoffment to Duke of Chaoxian.

sourceUnits.zh: 廆卒，嗣位，以平北將軍行平州刺史，督攝部內。
sourceUnits.en: When Hui died he succeeded him, serving as general who pacifies the north and acting governor of Pingzhou with authority over the whole command.
sourceUnits.literal: When Hui died, he succeeded the position; as general who pacifies the north acted as governor of Ping Province, supervising and holding the interior of the command.

sourceUnits.zh: 尋而宇文乞得龜為其別部逸豆歸所逐，奔死於外，皝率騎討之，逸豆歸懼而請和，遂築榆陰、安晉二城而還。
sourceUnits.en: Soon afterward Yuwen Qidegui was driven out by Yidougui of his separate division and died in exile; Huang led cavalry against Yidougui, who took fright and sued for peace; Huang then built the two cities of Yuyin and Anjin and withdrew.
sourceUnits.literal: Soon Yuwen Qidegui was by his separate division Yidougui expelled, fled and died outside; Huang led cavalry to campaign against him; Yidougui feared and requested peace; thereupon built the two cities of Yuyin and Anjin and returned.

sourceUnits.zh: 初，皝庶兄建威翰驍武有雄才，素為皝所忌，母弟征虜仁、廣武昭並有寵於廆，皝亦不平之。
sourceUnits.en: Earlier, Huang's elder half-brother Murong Han, general who establishes might, was brave in arms and of heroic talent, and Huang had long resented him. Huang's younger full brothers Murong Ren, general who campaigns against the caitiffs, and Murong Zhao, general who extends martial power, were both favored by Hui, which also displeased Huang.
sourceUnits.literal: At first, Huang's elder brother by a concubine, Han, the general who establishes might, was brave in warfare and had heroic talent; Huang had long been jealous of him. His younger brothers by the same mother, Ren, the general who campaigns against the caitiffs, and Zhao, the general who extends martial power, both enjoyed Hui's favor; Huang was also displeased with them.

sourceUnits.zh: 及廆卒，並懼不自容。
sourceUnits.en: When Hui died they all feared for their lives.
sourceUnits.literal: When Hui died, all feared they could not preserve themselves.

sourceUnits.zh: 至此，翰出奔段遼，仁勸昭舉兵廢皝。
sourceUnits.en: Murong Han fled to Duan Liao, while Murong Ren urged Murong Zhao to revolt and depose Huang.
sourceUnits.literal: Reaching this point, Han fled out to Duan Liao; Ren urged Zhao to raise troops and depose Huang.

sourceUnits.zh: 皝殺昭，遣使按檢仁之虛實，遇仁於險瀆。
sourceUnits.en: Huang executed Zhao and sent envoys to probe whether Ren’s situation was genuine; they encountered Ren at Xiandu.
sourceUnits.literal: Huang killed Zhao, sent envoys to investigate the truth of Ren’s situation, met Ren at Xiandu.

sourceUnits.zh: 仁知事發，殺皝使，東歸平郭。
sourceUnits.en: Ren saw his plot exposed, killed the messenger, and fled east to Pingguo.
sourceUnits.literal: Ren knew the affair had broken; killed Huang’s envoy; went east to return to Pingguo.

sourceUnits.zh: 皝遣其弟建武幼、司馬佟壽等討之。
sourceUnits.en: Huang dispatched his younger brother Murong You, general who establishes martial power, Marshal Tong Shou, and others to campaign against Ren.
sourceUnits.literal: Huang sent his younger brother You, the general who establishes martial power, marshal Tong Shou, and others to campaign against him.

sourceUnits.zh: 仁盡眾距戰，幼等大敗，皆沒於仁。
sourceUnits.en: Ren threw his whole army into the fight and crushed You’s force, capturing every commander.
sourceUnits.literal: Ren exhausted the host to resist battle; You and the others were greatly defeated, all lost to Ren.

sourceUnits.zh: 襄平令王冰、將軍孫機以遼東叛於皝，東夷校尉封抽、護軍乙逸、遼東相韓矯、玄菟太守高詡等棄城奔還。
sourceUnits.en: Xiangping magistrate Wang Bing and general Sun Ji rebelled in Liaodong against Huang; Eastern Yi Colonel Feng Chou, Protector Yi Yi, Liaodong chancellor Han Jiao, Xuantu prefect Gao Xu, and others abandoned their cities and fled back.
sourceUnits.literal: Xiangping magistrate Wang Bing and general Sun Ji rebelled in Liaodong against Huang; Eastern Yi Colonel Feng Chou, protector Yi Yi, Liaodong chancellor Han Jiao, Xuantu prefect Gao Xu, and others abandoned cities and fled back.

sourceUnits.zh: 仁於是盡有遼左之地，自稱車騎將軍、平州刺史、遼東公。
sourceUnits.en: Ren then controlled all territory east of the Liao, proclaiming himself general of chariots and cavalry, governor of Pingzhou, and duke of Liaodong.
sourceUnits.literal: Ren thereupon wholly possessed the land left of the Liao, styled himself General of Chariots and Cavalry, governor of Ping Province, Duke of Liaodong.

sourceUnits.zh: 宇文歸、段遼及鮮卑諸部並為之援，
sourceUnits.en: Yuwen Gui, Duan Liao, and other Xianbei chiefs backed him.
sourceUnits.literal: Yuwen Gui, Duan Liao, and the various Xianbei divisions all became his aid.

sourceUnits.zh: 皝乃令曰：「覽封記室之諫，孤實懼焉。
sourceUnits.en: Huang then issued an order, saying: “On reading the remonstrance of Recorder Feng, I am truly afraid.
sourceUnits.literal: Huang thereupon ordered, saying: “Having read Secretary Feng’s remonstrance, I truly fear it.

sourceUnits.zh: 君以黎元為國，黎元以穀為命。
sourceUnits.en: The ruler exists for his people; the people live on grain.
sourceUnits.literal: The lord takes the black-haired people as the state; the black-haired people take grain as life.

sourceUnits.zh: 然則農者，國之本也，而二千石令長不遵孟春之令，惰農弗勸，宜以尤不修辟者措之刑法，肅厲屬城。
sourceUnits.en: Agriculture is the foundation, yet magistrates ignore spring plowing—those who leave fields idle should face punishment to wake the commanderies.
sourceUnits.literal: Then farming is the state’s root, yet two-thousand-bushel magistrates and county chiefs do not obey the first month’s orders, lazy farmers are not urged—ought with blame on those who do not cultivate wasteland apply to them criminal law, to awe and encourage dependent cities.

sourceUnits.zh: 主者明詳推檢，具狀以聞。
sourceUnits.en: Let bureaus audit every case and report in full.
sourceUnits.literal: Let the responsible officials clearly examine and push investigation, submit full reports to be heard.

sourceUnits.zh: 苑囿悉可罷之，以給百姓無田業者。
sourceUnits.en: Close the hunting reserves and give that land to landless peasants.
sourceUnits.literal: Hunting parks all can be abolished, to give to common people without fields or occupations.

sourceUnits.zh: 貧者全無資產，不能自存，各賜牧牛一頭。
sourceUnits.en: Give each destitute household a draft ox.
sourceUnits.literal: Poor persons wholly lack assets, cannot preserve themselves—each grant one herding ox.

sourceUnits.zh: 若私有餘力，樂取官牛墾官田者，其依魏、晉舊法。
sourceUnits.en: Whoever wishes to rent state oxen and state land may do so under Wei–Jin precedent.
sourceUnits.literal: If private surplus strength, happy to take official oxen to reclaim official fields, let it follow Wei and Jin old laws.

sourceUnits.zh: 溝洫溉灌，有益官私，主者量造，務盡水陸之勢。
sourceUnits.en: Dig irrigation works for public and private good—let engineers plan every channel.
sourceUnits.literal: Ditches and channels irrigation pour, benefit public and private; let the responsible officials measure and build, exhaust the advantage of water and land.

sourceUnits.zh: 中州未平，兵難不息，勳誠既多，官僚不可以減也。
sourceUnits.en: The heartland is not yet pacified, warfare does not cease, and many have rendered meritorious and loyal service, so the official establishment cannot be reduced.
sourceUnits.literal: The central plain is not yet pacified; military difficulty does not cease; merit and loyalty are already many—bureaucracy cannot be reduced.

sourceUnits.zh: 待克平凶醜，徐更議之。
sourceUnits.en: We will revisit staff cuts after victory.
sourceUnits.literal: Wait until we crush the villains, slowly again deliberate it.

sourceUnits.zh: 百工商賈數，四佐與列將速定大員，余者還農。
sourceUnits.en: Cap tradesmen and aides to fixed quotas; everyone else goes back to the plow.
sourceUnits.literal: Hundred crafts and merchants’ numbers, four assistants and column generals quickly fix great quotas; the rest return to farming.

sourceUnits.zh: 學生不任訓教者，亦除員錄。
sourceUnits.en: Strike idle students from the rolls.
sourceUnits.literal: Students who do not bear training and teaching, also remove from rolls.

sourceUnits.zh: 夫人臣關言於人主，至難也，妖妄不經之事皆應蕩然不問，擇其善者而從之。
sourceUnits.en: For a minister to offer words that touch his ruler is most difficult; wild and baseless matters should all be brushed aside without inquiry, while one chooses what is good and follows it.
sourceUnits.literal: For a minister to present words to his sovereign is most difficult; absurd and unfounded matters should all be set aside without inquiry, while one chooses what is good and follows it.

sourceUnits.zh: 王憲、劉明雖其罪應禁黜，亦猶孤之無大量也。
sourceUnits.en: Wang Xian and Liu Ming, although their offenses would warrant ban and dismissal, also show my own lack of forbearance.
sourceUnits.literal: Wang Xian and Liu Ming although their crimes ought to be banned and dismissed, also is my lacking great measure.

sourceUnits.zh: 可悉復本官，仍居諫司。
sourceUnits.en: They may all be restored to their original offices and still serve in the remonstrance bureau.
sourceUnits.literal: Can all restore original offices, still dwell in remonstrance offices.

sourceUnits.zh: 封生蹇蹇，深得王臣之體。
sourceUnits.en: Feng Yu spoke as a true minister should.
sourceUnits.literal: Feng Sheng staunchly upright, deeply attained the body of a royal minister.

sourceUnits.zh: 《詩》不云乎：'無言不酬。
sourceUnits.en: As the Odes says, “No word goes unanswered.”
sourceUnits.literal: The Odes does it not say: “No word without answer.”

sourceUnits.zh: '其賜錢五萬，明宣內外，有欲陳孤過者，不拘貴賤，勿有所諱。」
sourceUnits.en: So award him fifty thousand cash, and clearly announce inside and outside that whoever wishes to state my faults, whether noble or base, need have no taboo.”
sourceUnits.literal: Grant cash fifty thousand; clearly proclaim inside and outside: whoever wishes to state my faults, not constrained noble or base, do not have what is taboo.”

sourceUnits.zh: 時有黑龍、白龍各一，見於龍山，皝親率群僚觀之，去龍二百餘步，祭乙太宰。
sourceUnits.en: A black dragon and a white dragon appeared on Long Mountain; Huang led his court within two hundred paces and offered the great sacrifice.
sourceUnits.literal: At the time there were black dragon and white dragon each one, appeared at Long Mountain; Huang personally led the group of officials to observe them, two hundred-odd steps from the dragons, sacrificed with the grand boar offering.

sourceUnits.zh: 二龍交首嬉翔，解角而去。
sourceUnits.en: The two dragons crossed their heads, sported and soared, shed their horns, and departed.
sourceUnits.literal: The two dragons crossed heads, sported and soared, shed horns and departed.

sourceUnits.zh: 皝大悅，還宮，赦其境內，號新宮曰和龍，立龍翔佛寺於山上。
sourceUnits.en: Huang was greatly pleased, returned to the palace, pardoned those within his borders, named the new palace Helong, and built the Longxiang Buddhist monastery on the mountain.
sourceUnits.literal: Huang was greatly pleased, returned to the palace, pardoned those within his borders, named the new palace Helong, and established the Longxiang Buddhist temple on the mountain.

sourceUnits.zh: 賜其大臣子弟為官學生者號高門生，立東庠于舊宮，以行鄉射之禮，每月臨觀，考試優劣。
sourceUnits.en: He labeled elite students “high-gate pupils,” reopened the eastern school for archery rites, and each month examined their progress.
sourceUnits.literal: Granted his great ministers’ sons and younger brothers who were official students the title “high-gate students,” set up the eastern school in the old palace, to perform the village archery rite, each month personally observing, examining excellence and inferiority.

sourceUnits.zh: 皝雅好文籍，勤于講授，學徒甚盛，至千餘人。
sourceUnits.en: He loved books, lectured tirelessly, and kept more than a thousand students.
sourceUnits.literal: Huang by nature loved documents and records, diligent in lecturing and teaching; students were extremely many, reaching over a thousand persons.

sourceUnits.zh: 親造《太上章》以代《急就》，又著《典誡》十五篇，以教胄子。
sourceUnits.en: He personally composed the Taishang Chapter to replace the Jijiu, and also wrote fifteen chapters of Canonical Admonitions to teach the sons of the nobility.
sourceUnits.literal: He personally composed the Taishang Chapter to replace the Jijiu, and also wrote fifteen chapters of Canonical Admonitions, to teach the sons of the nobility.

sourceUnits.zh: 慕容恪攻高句麗南蘇，克之，置戍而還。
sourceUnits.en: Murong Ke attacked Goguryeo’s Nansu, took it, posted a garrison, and returned.
sourceUnits.literal: Murong Ke attacked Goguryeo’s Nansu, took it, set garrison and returned.

sourceUnits.zh: 三年，遣其世子俊與恪率騎萬七千東襲夫餘，克之，虜其王及部眾五萬餘口以還。
sourceUnits.en: In the third year he sent his heir Jun and Ke with seventeen thousand cavalry to raid Puyu eastward; they took it, captured its king and more than fifty thousand of the tribe, and returned.
sourceUnits.literal: In the third year, sent his heir apparent Jun with Ke leading cavalry seventeen thousand east to raid Puyu, took it, captured their king and division host over fifty thousand mouths and returned.

sourceUnits.zh: 皝親臨東庠考試學生，其經通秀異者，擢充近侍。
sourceUnits.en: He tested students at the eastern school and promoted the best as attendants.
sourceUnits.literal: Huang personally arrived at the eastern school to examine students; those whose classics were thorough and outstanding, promoted to fill close attendance.

sourceUnits.zh: 以久旱，丐百姓田租。
sourceUnits.en: He remitted rent during a drought.
sourceUnits.literal: Because of long drought, begged off common people’s field rent.

sourceUnits.zh: 罷成周、冀陽、營丘等郡。
sourceUnits.en: He abolished several empty commanderies such as Chengzhou, Jiyang, and Yingqiu.
sourceUnits.literal: Abolished Chengzhou, Jiyang, Yingqiu, and other commanderies.

sourceUnits.zh: 以勃海人為興集縣，河間人為寧集縣，廣平、魏郡人為興平縣，東萊、北海人為育黎縣，吳人為吳縣，悉隸燕國。
sourceUnits.en: He grouped refugees from Bohai, Hejian, Guangping, Wei, Donglai, Beihai, and Wu into new counties under Yan.
sourceUnits.literal: Made Bohai people Xingji county, Hejian people Ningji county, Guangping and Wei commandery people Xingping county, Donglai and Beihai people Yuli county, Wu people Wu county—all subordinate to the state of Yan.

sourceUnits.zh: 皝嘗畋於西鄙，將濟河，見一父老，服硃衣，乘白馬，舉手麾皝曰：「此非獵所，王其還也。」
sourceUnits.en: While hunting on the western frontier Murong Huang was about to cross a river when he saw an old man in cinnabar robes on a white horse, who waved him off and said, "This is not a place for hunting; Your Majesty should return."
sourceUnits.literal: Huang once hunted on the western border, about to cross the River, saw an old man, dressed cinnabar robes, riding a white horse, raised hand and waved Huang, saying: “This is not a hunting place; the king ought to return.”

sourceUnits.zh: 秘之不言，遂濟河，連日大獲。
sourceUnits.en: He kept silent, crossed the river, and enjoyed great sport for days.
sourceUnits.literal: He concealed it and did not speak, thereupon crossed the River, continuously days great catch.

sourceUnits.zh: 後見白兔，馳射之，馬倒被傷，乃說所見。
sourceUnits.en: Later he charged a white hare, was thrown and hurt, and told the omen.
sourceUnits.literal: Later saw white hare, galloped and shot it; horse fell and he was injured, then narrated what he had seen.

sourceUnits.zh: 輦而還宮，引俊屬以後事。
sourceUnits.en: They carried him home; he briefed Murong Jun on the succession.
sourceUnits.literal: Carried on litter returned palace, led Jun to entrust later affairs.

sourceUnits.zh: 以永和四年死，在位十五年，時年五十二。
sourceUnits.en: He died in Yonghe 4 (348 CE) after fifteen years on the throne, aged fifty-two.
sourceUnits.literal: Died in the fourth year of Yonghe, fifteen years on the throne, age fifty-two sui.

sourceUnits.zh: 俊僭號，追諡文明皇帝。
sourceUnits.en: After Murong Jun took the throne he posthumously styled his father Emperor Wenming.
sourceUnits.literal: When Jun illegitimately assumed imperial title, posthumously honored him as Emperor Wenming.

sourceUnits.zh: 慕容翰
sourceUnits.en: Murong Han (defector general).
sourceUnits.literal: Murong Han.

sourceUnits.zh: 慕容翰，字元邕，廆之庶長子也。
sourceUnits.en: Murong Han, courtesy name Yuanyong, was Murong Hui’s eldest son by a concubine.
sourceUnits.literal: Murong Han, courtesy name Yuanyong, was Hui’s eldest son by a concubine.

sourceUnits.zh: 性雄豪，多權略，猿臂工射，膂力過人。
sourceUnits.en: He was bold, cunning, a superb archer, and immensely strong.
sourceUnits.literal: Nature heroic and bold, abundant in stratagem; ape arms skilled at shooting; physical strength surpassed others.

sourceUnits.zh: 廆甚奇之，委以折沖之任。
sourceUnits.en: Murong Hui prized him and gave him the hardest fighting assignments.
sourceUnits.literal: Hui greatly wondered at him, entrusted him with the charge of breaking the enemy’s momentum.

sourceUnits.zh: 行師征伐，所在有功，威聲大振，為遠近所憚。
sourceUnits.en: Every campaign brought success; neighbors far and near feared him.
sourceUnits.literal: When lines marched and campaigned, wherever he went had merit; awe-inspiring name greatly shook, feared by far and near.

sourceUnits.zh: 作鎮遼東，高句麗不敢為寇。
sourceUnits.en: While he held Liaodong, Goguryeo dared not raid.
sourceUnits.literal: As garrison commander in Liaodong, Goguryeo did not dare make raids.

sourceUnits.zh: 善撫接，愛儒學，自士大夫至於卒伍，莫不樂而從之。
sourceUnits.en: He won men from gentry to ranks by kindness and a love of learning.
sourceUnits.literal: Skilled at comforting and drawing near, loved classical learning; from grandees down to common soldiers, none did not joyfully follow him.

sourceUnits.zh: 及奔段遼，深為遼所敬愛。
sourceUnits.en: Duan Liao honored him after his defection.
sourceUnits.literal: When he fled to Duan Liao, deeply was respected and loved by Liao.

sourceUnits.zh: 柳城之敗，段蘭欲乘勝深入，翰慮成本國之害，詭說于蘭，蘭遂不進。
sourceUnits.en: After the defeat at Liucheng, Duan Lan wanted to push on, but Murong Han feigned advice that spared Yan a deeper strike.
sourceUnits.literal: At Liucheng’s defeat, Duan Lan wished to ride victory to penetrate deep; Han worried it would complete harm to his native state, deceitfully spoke to Lan; Lan then did not advance.

sourceUnits.zh: 後石季龍征遼，皝親將三軍略令支以北，遼議欲追之，翰知皝躬自總戎，戰必克勝，乃謂遼曰：「今石氏向至，方對大故，不宜復以小小為事。
sourceUnits.en: Later when Shi Hu campaigned against Duan Liao and Murong Huang personally led an army to raid north of Lingzhi, Duan Liao debated pursuit. Knowing Huang commanded in person and must win, Murong Han told Duan Liao, "Now the Shi are about to arrive and you face a great enemy; you should not again take up small matters.
sourceUnits.literal: Later Shi Jilong campaigned against Liao; Huang personally led the three armies raiding north of Lingzhi; Liao debated wishing to pursue him; Han knew Huang personally commanded the army, battle must seize victory; thereupon said to Liao: “Now the Shi clan is about to arrive, just facing great enemy; ought not again to take small matters as affairs.

sourceUnits.zh: 燕王自來，士馬精銳。
sourceUnits.en: Murong Huang’s host is elite.
sourceUnits.literal: The King of Yan has come in person; soldiers and horses are picked and sharp.

sourceUnits.zh: 兵者凶器，戰有危慮，若其失利，何以南禦乎！」
sourceUnits.en: War is peril—if you lose here, how will you hold the south?”
sourceUnits.literal: Weapons are ill-omened tools; battle has perilous anxiety; if it misses advantage, how to defend the south!”

sourceUnits.zh: 蘭怒曰：「吾前聽卿誑說，致成今患，不復入卿計中矣。」
sourceUnits.en: Duan Lan snapped, “Your last ‘advice’ ruined me—I will not heed you again.”
sourceUnits.literal: Lan angrily said: “Formerly I listened to your deceitful talk, caused to complete today’s disaster; I do not again enter your schemes.”

sourceUnits.zh: 乃率眾追皝，蘭果大敗。
sourceUnits.en: He chased Huang and was crushed.
sourceUnits.literal: Thereupon led host to pursue Huang; Lan was indeed greatly defeated.

sourceUnits.zh: 翰雖處仇國，因事立忠，皆此類也。
sourceUnits.en: Even in exile Murong Han worked secretly for Yan’s good.
sourceUnits.literal: Although Han dwelt in an enemy state, by events established loyalty—all was of this kind.

sourceUnits.zh: 及遼奔走，翰又北投宇文歸。
sourceUnits.en: When Duan Liao fled in defeat, Han again went north to Yuwen Gui.
sourceUnits.literal: When Liao fled in defeat, Han again north threw himself to Yuwen Gui.

sourceUnits.zh: 既而逃，歸乃遣勁騎百餘追之。
sourceUnits.en: Yuwen Gui sent a hundred picked riders after him.
sourceUnits.literal: Having then fled, Gui thereupon sent fierce cavalry over a hundred to pursue him.

sourceUnits.zh: 翰遙謂追者曰：「吾既思戀而歸，理無反面。
sourceUnits.en: He shouted to them, “I mean to go home—I will not turn back.
sourceUnits.literal: Han from afar told the pursuers: “I already long to return; in principle there is no turning back.

sourceUnits.zh: 吾之弓矢，汝曹足知，無為相逼，自取死也。
sourceUnits.en: You know my archery—do not force a fight.
sourceUnits.literal: My bow and arrows, you lot fully know; do not force each other, self-seeking death.

sourceUnits.zh: 吾處汝國久，恨不殺汝。
sourceUnits.en: I have lived among you too long—I should have killed you.
sourceUnits.literal: I have dwelt in your state long; I regret not killing you.

sourceUnits.zh: 汝可百步豎刀，吾射中者，汝便宜反；
sourceUnits.en: Plant a blade at a hundred paces—if I ring it, withdraw;
sourceUnits.literal: You can at a hundred paces set up a blade; if I shoot the center, you then conveniently turn back;

sourceUnits.zh: 不中者，可來前也。」
sourceUnits.en: if I miss, come on.”
sourceUnits.literal: if not center, you may come forward.”

sourceUnits.zh: 歸騎解刀豎之，翰一發便中刀鐶，追騎乃散。
sourceUnits.en: They fixed a blade; his first arrow struck the ring and they broke off the chase.
sourceUnits.literal: Gui’s riders undid a blade and set it up; Han one shot then hit the blade ring; pursuing riders then scattered.

sourceUnits.zh: 既至，皝甚加恩禮，
sourceUnits.en: Huang welcomed him with rich honors.
sourceUnits.literal: Having arrived, Huang greatly added favor and ceremony.

sourceUnits.zh: 建元二年，從皝討宇文歸，臨陣為流矢所中，臥病積時。
sourceUnits.en: In the second year of Jianyuan, he joined the war on Yuwen Gui, took a stray shaft, and lay long ill.
sourceUnits.literal: In the second year of Jianyuan, he followed Huang to campaign against Yuwen Gui; on the line of battle he was struck by a stray arrow; he lay ill a long time.

sourceUnits.zh: 後疾漸愈，於其家中騎馬自試，或有人告翰私習騎，疑為非常。
sourceUnits.en: When he tried riding at home, informers called it sedition.
sourceUnits.literal: Later illness gradually improved; at his home mounted horse to test himself; someone reported Han privately practiced riding, suspected as unusual.

sourceUnits.zh: 皝素忌之，遂賜死焉。
sourceUnits.en: Huang, who had always feared him, sent him poison.
sourceUnits.literal: Huang plain envied him; thereupon granted death.

sourceUnits.zh: 翰臨死謂使者曰：「翰懷疑外奔，罪不容誅，不能以骸骨委賊庭，故歸罪有司。
sourceUnits.en: Murong Han told the messenger, “I fled in fear and deserved death, yet I would not die in a foreign hall, so I came home to face judgment.
sourceUnits.literal: Han nearing death told the envoy: “Han harbored suspicion and fled abroad; crime does not permit execution; could not cast bones in the bandit court; therefore returned guilt to the responsible officials.

sourceUnits.zh: 天慈曲湣，不肆之市朝，今日之死，翰之生也。
sourceUnits.en: The king spared me a public execution—this death is mercy.
sourceUnits.literal: Heaven’s kindness bent pity, did not display me in the marketplace; today’s death is Han’s life.

sourceUnits.zh: 但逆胡跨據神州，中原未靖，翰常克心自誓，志吞醜虜，上成先王遺旨，下謝山海之責。
sourceUnits.en: But the rebel Hu barbarians straddle and hold the Divine Land, and the Central Plain is not yet pacified. I always steeled my heart and swore that I would swallow up the vile caitiffs, above to fulfil the late king's dying wish and below to discharge my duty to the realm between the mountains and the sea.
sourceUnits.literal: But the rebellious Hu occupy the Divine Land, and the Central Plain is not yet pacified; Han has always steeled his heart and sworn an oath, intent on swallowing up the vile enemies, above to fulfil the late king's last instructions and below to discharge his duty to the land of mountains and seas.

sourceUnits.zh: 不圖此心不遂，沒有餘恨，命也奈何！」
sourceUnits.en: That hope dies with me—such is fate.”
sourceUnits.literal: Did not expect this heart not to succeed; dying there is surplus regret—fate it—what to do!”

sourceUnits.zh: 仰藥而死。
sourceUnits.en: He drank the poison and died.
sourceUnits.literal: Raised poison and died.

sourceUnits.zh: 陽裕
sourceUnits.en: Yang Yu.
sourceUnits.literal: Yang Yu.

sourceUnits.zh: 陽裕，字士倫，右北平無終人也。
sourceUnits.en: Yang Yu, courtesy name Shilun, came from Wuzhong in right Beiping.
sourceUnits.literal: Yang Yu, courtesy name Shilun, was a man of Wuzhong in Right Beiping.

sourceUnits.zh: 少孤，兄弟皆早亡，單煢獨立，雖宗族無能識者，惟叔父耽幼而奇之，曰：「此兒非惟吾門之標秀，乃佐時之良器也。」
sourceUnits.en: Orphaned young, with brothers dead early, he stood alone; few in the clan knew him, but his uncle Dan marveled at him even in youth and said, "This child is not only our clan's outstanding ornament but an instrument to serve the age."
sourceUnits.literal: In youth orphaned, brothers all died early, alone and solitary; although the lineage group none could recognize him, only uncle Dan in youth wondered at him, saying: “This child is not only our gate’s outstanding show, but an instrument to aid the age.”

sourceUnits.zh: 刺史和演辟為主簿。
sourceUnits.en: Governor He Yan made him chief clerk.
sourceUnits.literal: The governor He Yan summoned him as chief clerk.

sourceUnits.zh: 王浚領州，轉治中從事，忌而不能任。
sourceUnits.en: Under Wang Jun he rose to administration aide but was distrusted.
sourceUnits.literal: Wang Jun held the province, transferred to aide in the bureau of administration, envied yet could not employ him.

nameClaims.en: younger brother by the same mother
younger brother by the same mother

knownProposedCorrections.before: A black dragon and a white dragon appeared on Long Mountain; Huang led his court within two hundred paces and offered the great sacrifice.
knownProposedCorrections.after: A black dragon and a white dragon appeared on Long Mountain; Huang personally led his officials to observe them from more than two hundred paces away and offered a tailao sacrifice.
knownProposedCorrections.sourceReason: 去龍二百餘步 means more than two hundred paces away, not within two hundred. The complete primary passage reads 祭以太牢, whereas the supplied Chinese field has the anomalous 祭乙太宰; this English correction does not silently amend that Chinese field.
knownProposedCorrections.sourceChinese: 時有黑龍、白龍各一，見於龍山，皝親率群僚觀之，去龍二百餘步，祭乙太宰。

knownProposedCorrections.before: At the time there were black dragon and white dragon each one, appeared at Long Mountain; Huang personally led the group of officials to observe them, two hundred-odd steps from the dragons, sacrificed with the grand boar offering.
knownProposedCorrections.after: At the time, one black dragon and one white dragon appeared on Long Mountain. Huang personally led the assembled officials to observe them from more than two hundred paces away and sacrificed with a tailao offering.
knownProposedCorrections.sourceReason: The linked complete text has 祭以太牢, also corroborated in Tongjian’s 345 dragon notice. 太牢 is not a grand boar offering. The supplied Chinese 祭乙太宰 is a separate textual discrepancy and is not changed here.
knownProposedCorrections.sourceChinese: 時有黑龍、白龍各一，見於龍山，皝親率群僚觀之，去龍二百餘步，祭乙太宰。

knownProposedCorrections.before: He labeled elite students “high-gate pupils,” reopened the eastern school for archery rites, and each month examined their progress.
knownProposedCorrections.after: He gave the sons and younger brothers of his senior ministers who were official students the title “high-gate students,” established the eastern school in the old palace for the village archery rites, and personally observed and assessed their performance each month.
knownProposedCorrections.sourceReason: 立東庠于舊宮 establishes a school in the old palace; it does not say reopened. The fuller wording also preserves the official-student qualification and the kinship group receiving the title.
knownProposedCorrections.sourceChinese: 賜其大臣子弟為官學生者號高門生，立東庠于舊宮，以行鄉射之禮，每月臨觀，考試優劣。

knownProposedCorrections.before: Because of long drought, begged off common people’s field rent.
knownProposedCorrections.after: Because of the prolonged drought, he remitted the common people’s field tax.
knownProposedCorrections.sourceReason: 丐百姓田租 in this governmental context grants remission of field tax; begged off misstates the ruler’s action and its recipient. The en field already represents remission and needs no corresponding change.

knownProposedCorrections.before: He abolished several empty commanderies such as Chengzhou, Jiyang, and Yingqiu.
knownProposedCorrections.after: He abolished Chengzhou, Jiyang, Yingqiu, and other commanderies.
knownProposedCorrections.sourceReason: 罷成周、冀陽、營丘等郡 does not describe the commanderies as empty. Remove that unsupported characterization; the literal field already preserves the unqualified abolition.

knownProposedCorrections.before: They carried him home; he briefed Murong Jun on the succession.
knownProposedCorrections.after: He was carried back to the palace in a litter and summoned Jun to entrust him with affairs after his death.
knownProposedCorrections.sourceReason: 引俊屬以後事 describes summoning Jun and entrusting him with subsequent affairs, not merely briefing him on succession; 宮 is the palace, and 輦 specifies litter conveyance.
knownProposedCorrections.sourceChinese: 輦而還宮，引俊屬以後事。

knownProposedCorrections.before: Carried on litter returned palace, led Jun to entrust later affairs.
knownProposedCorrections.after: He returned to the palace in a litter and summoned Jun, entrusting him with affairs after his death.
knownProposedCorrections.sourceReason: 引俊 here summons Jun; 屬以後事 entrusts him with the affairs to follow the dying ruler, as the next sentence confirms. Led Jun to entrust later affairs obscures who entrusts whom.
knownProposedCorrections.sourceChinese: 輦而還宮，引俊屬以後事。

knownProposedCorrections.before: After Murong Jun took the throne he posthumously styled his father Emperor Wenming.
knownProposedCorrections.after: When Murong Jun assumed the imperial title in usurpation, he posthumously honored his father as Emperor Wenming.
knownProposedCorrections.sourceReason: 俊僭號 means Jun’s assumption of an imperial title, not his earlier succession to the throne. Preserve 僭 and avoid conflating the later imperial claim with succession after Huang’s death. The literal field already distinguishes this action.
